291: 			cfg.Resources.Add(istructsmem.NewCommandFunction(testQName, istructsmem.NullCommandExec))

302: 	f.fill(1002)
303: 	topOffset := f.fill(1001)
304: 
305: 	withCancel, cancelCtx := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
306: 	errors := make(chan string, 10)
307: 	chanAfterError := make(chan time.Time)
308: 
309: 	broker, cleanup := in10nmem.ProvideEx2(in10n.Quotas{
310: 		Channels:               2,
311: 		ChannelsPerSubject:     2,
312: 		Subsciptions:           2,

314: 	}, time.Now)
315: 	defer cleanup()
316: 
317: 	metrics := imetrics.Provide()
318: 	getProjectorsInError := func() float64 {
319: 		var projInErrors float64
320: 		metrics.List(func(metric imetrics.IMetric, metricValue float64) (err error) {
321: 			if metric.App() == istructs.AppQName_test1_app1 && metric.Vvm() == "test" && metric.Name() == ProjectorsInError {
322: 				projInErrors = metricValue
323: 			}

329: 	// init and launch actualizer

331: 		Ctx:        withCancel,
332: 		Partition:  partitionNr,
333: 		AppStructs: func() istructs.IAppStructs { return app },
334: 		AfterError: func(d time.Duration) <-chan time.Time {
335: 			if d.Seconds() != 30.0 {
336: 				panic("unexpected pause")
337: 			}
338: 			return chanAfterError
339: 		},
340: 		BundlesLimit:  10,
341: 		FlushInterval: 10 * time.Millisecond,
342: 		LogError: func(args ...interface{}) {
343: 			errors <- fmt.Sprint("error: ", args)
344: 		},
345: 		Broker:   broker,

348: 		AppQName: istructs.AppQName_test1_app1,

351: 
352: 	factory := func(partition istructs.PartitionID) istructs.Projector {
353: 		return istructs.Projector{Name: name, Func: func(event istructs.IPLogEvent, state istructs.IState, intents istructs.IIntents) (err error) {
354: 			if event.Workspace() == 1002 {
355: 				if attempts == 0 {
356: 					attempts++
357: 					return fmt.Errorf("test error") // First attempt will fail
358: 				}
359: 				attempts++
360: 			}
361: 			return nil
362: 		}}
363: 	}
364: 
365: 	actualizerFactory := ProvideAsyncActualizerFactory()
366: 	actualizer, err := actualizerFactory(conf, factory)
367: 	require.NoError(err)
368: 	require.NoError(actualizer.DoSync(conf.Ctx, struct{}{})) // Start service
369: 
370: 	// Wait for the logged error

376: 		time.Sleep(time.Microsecond)

384: 	// Now the istructs.Projector must handle the log till the end

505: 	return offset

603: func (m *simpleMetrics) Increase(metricName string, partition istructs.PartitionID, projection appdef.QName, valueDelta float64) {

616: 	} else if metricName == aaFlushesTotal {
617: 		atomic.StoreInt64(&m.flushesTotal, int64(value))
618: 	} else {
619: 		atomic.StoreInt64(&m.storedOffset, int64(value))
620: 	}

315: 		fileName := filepath.Base(entryPath)
316: 		// we can't have embed.FS of the dir with go.mod file inside,
317: 		// that's why we name it test.go.mod and rename it back
318: 		if fileName == "test.go.mod" {

324: 		}

The in-memory bus implementation (`ibusmem`) currently invokes the request handler callback without passing the bus instance itself. This forces the caller to capture the bus via a closure variable, which is awkward and error-prone — especially when the bus is created lazily or the handler needs to reference it directly for sending responses or parallel responses.

    We need to change the `Provide` and `provide` functions (and the underlying `bus` struct) so that the request handler callback receives the `ibus.IBus` instance as an additional parameter. The new handler signature should be:

71: 		if err != nil {
72: 			coreutils.ReplyAccessDeniedUnauthorized(bus, sender, err.Error())
73: 			return
74: 		}
75: 
76: 		deliverToProcessors(request, requestCtx, appQName, sender, funcType, procbus, bus, token, cpchIdx, qpcgIdx, cpAmount)
77: 	})
78: 	return bus

81: func deliverToProcessors(request ibus.Request, requestCtx context.Context, appQName istructs.AppQName, sender interface{}, funcType appdef.IType,
82: 	procbus iprocbus.IProcBus, bus ibus.IBus, token string, cpchIdx CommandProcessorsChannelGroupIdxType, qpcgIdx QueryProcessorsChannelGroupIdxType,
83: 	cpAmount coreutils.CommandProcessorsCount) {
84: 	switch request.Resource[:1] {
85: 	case "q":
86: 		iqm := queryprocessor.NewQueryMessage(requestCtx, appQName, istructs.WSID(request.WSID), sender, request.Body, funcType.(appdef.IQuery), request.Host, token)
87: 		if !procbus.Submit(int(qpcgIdx), 0, iqm) {
88: 			coreutils.ReplyErrf(bus, sender, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "no query processors available")
89: 		}
90: 	case "c":
91: 		channelIdx := request.WSID % int64(cpAmount)
92: 		partitionID := istructs.PartitionID(channelIdx)
93: 		icm := commandprocessor.NewCommandMessage(requestCtx, request.Body, appQName, istructs.WSID(request.WSID), sender, partitionID, funcType.(appdef.ICommand), token, request.Host)
94: 		if !procbus.Submit(int(cpchIdx), int(channelIdx), icm) {
95: 			coreutils.ReplyErrf(bus, sender, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, fmt.Sprintf("command processor of partition %d is busy", partitionID))
96: 		}
97: 	}
98: }

100: func getFuncType(as istructs.IAppStructs, qName appdef.QName, bus ibus.IBus, sender interface{}, funcKindMark string) (appdef.IType, bool) {
101: 	tp := as.AppDef().Type(qName)
102: 	switch tp.Kind() {
103: 	case appdef.TypeKind_null:
104: 		coreutils.ReplyBadRequest(bus, sender, "unknown function "+qName.String())
105: 		return nil, true
106: 	case appdef.TypeKind_Query:
107: 		if funcKindMark == "q" {
108: 			return tp, false
109: 		}
110: 	case appdef.TypeKind_Command:
111: 		if funcKindMark == "c" {
112: 			return tp, false
113: 		}
114: 	}
115: 	coreutils.ReplyBadRequest(bus, sender, fmt.Sprintf(`wrong function kind "%s" for function %s`, funcKindMark, qName))
116: 	return nil, true

119: func getPrincipalToken(request ibus.Request) (token string, err error) {
120: 	authHeaders := request.Header[coreutils.Authorization]
121: 	if len(authHeaders) == 0 {
122: 		return "", nil
123: 	}
124: 	authHeader := authHeaders[0]
125: 	if strings.HasPrefix(authHeader, coreutils.BearerPrefix) {
126: 		return strings.ReplaceAll(authHeader, coreutils.BearerPrefix, ""), nil
127: 	}
128: 	if strings.HasPrefix(authHeader, "Basic ") {
129: 		return getBasicAuthToken(authHeader)
130: 	}
131: 	return "", errors.New("unsupported Authorization header: " + authHeader)
132: }
133: 
134: func getBasicAuthToken(authHeader string) (token string, err error) {
135: 	headerValue := strings.ReplaceAll(authHeader, "Basic ", "")
136: 	headerValueBytes, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(headerValue)
137: 	if err != nil {
138: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to decode base64 Basic Authorization header value: %w", err)
139: 	}
140: 	headerValue = string(headerValueBytes)
141: 	if strings.Count(headerValue, ":") != 1 {
142: 		return "", errors.New("unexpected Basic Authorization header format")
143: 	}
144: 	return strings.ReplaceAll(headerValue, ":", ""), nil
145: }

### Bus

- Bus connects system services
  - E.g.: HTTP Server, EMail Gateway, App Partition Query Handler
- For CE/SE services are located in the same process

### Principles

- Limited number of concurrent requests: maxNumOfConcurrentRequests
  - Example: million of http connections but 1000 concurrent requests
  - "ibus.ErrBusUnavailable" (503) is returned if the number of concurrent requests is exceeded
- Sender and Receiver both respect timeouts: readWriteTimeout
  - E.g. 5 seconds, by (weak) analogy with [FoundationDB, Long-running read/write transactions](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/anti-features.html)
- Result of QuerySender can be used even if AddressHandler has not been found - Sender will return `ErrReceiverNotFound` error

### Components

```mermaid
erDiagram
    ISender }|--|| Address : sends-to
    Address ||--|| AddressHandler : handled-by
    AddressHandler ||--|{ Processor : has
    Address ||--|| Receiver: associated-with

    Processor ||--|| Goroutine: has
    Processor }|--|| Receiver: has
    Goroutine }|--|| Receiver: calls    
```

### How it works with Commands and Queries

```mermaid
erDiagram
    HTTPClient ||--|| ISender_1: "requested ISender for sys/registry/8/q"
    ISender_1 ||--|| Address_1: connected-to
```

40: 	for i := 0; i < len(v1Components) || i < len(v2Components); i++ {

49: 		}

52: 			return 1

54: 			return -1

57:

59: }

2: # Copyright (c) 2023 Sigma-Soft, Ltd.
3: # @author Aleksei Ponomarev
4: #
5: # Backup scylla node. Execute command over ssh
6: # Usage: ./backupnode.sh <Node> <Target folder> <Path to ssh key>
7: # Example: ./backupnode.sh 127.0.0.1 /tmp/backup /home/user/.ssh/id_rsa
8: # Operations:
9: #  - Init
10: #    - get container id
11: #    - create signal file
12: #    - get avail keyspaces
13: #  - Backup
14: #    - take snapshot
15: #    - upload snapshot data
16: #    - dump schema
17: #  - By trap
18: #    - remove signal file
19: #    - clear snapshot
20: 
21: set -euo pipefail
22: 
23: if [[ $# -ne 3 ]]; then
24:   echo "Usage: $0 <Node> <Target folder> <Path to ssh key>"
25:   exit 1
26: fi
27: 
28: source ./utils.sh
29: source ./utils-cql.sh
30: 
31: readonly node=$1
32: readonly targetFolder=$2
33: readonly containerName="scylla"
34: readonly nodeDataDir="/var/lib/scylla"
35: readonly sshKey=$3
36: 
37: 
38: signalFile() {
39:     case "$1" in
40:         create)
41:             # Create the directory if it doesn't exist
42:             utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" mkdir -p "$(dirname "$signalFilePath")"
43: 
44:             # Create the signal file
45:             utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" touch "$signalFilePath"
46:             echo "Signal file created at: $signalFilePath"
47:             ;;
48:         remove)
49:             # Remove the signal file if it exists
50:             if utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" "[ -e $signalFilePath ]"; then
51:                 utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" rm "$signalFilePath"
52:                 echo "Signal file removed from: $signalFilePath"
53:             else
54:                 echo "Signal file not found at: $signalFilePath"
55:             fi
56:             ;;
57:         *)
58:             echo "Invalid operation. Use 'create' or 'remove'."
59:             ;;
60:     esac
61: }
62: 
63: snapshotTag() {
64:     local timeFormat="%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S"
65:     date +"$timeFormat"
66: }
67: 
68: snapshotCtl() {
69:     local operation="$1"
70: 
71:     local output
72:     local err
73: 
74:     if [ "$operation" != "snapshot" ] && [ "$operation" != "clearsnapshot" ]; then
75:       echo "Invalid operation. Use 'snapshot' or 'clearsnapshot'."
76:       return 1
77:     fi
78:     utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" "docker exec $container nodetool $operation -t $snapshotTag"
79:     echo "Snapshot $operation for node $node"
80:     err=$?
81: 
82:     if [ $err -ne 0 ]; then
83:         echo "Error taking snapshot: $output"
84:         return 1
85:     fi
86: 
87:     echo "$snapshotTag"
88: }
89: 
90: 
91: upload() {
92:     while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
93:         local keyspace="$1"
94:             shift
95:         utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" "mkdir -p $targetFolder/$keyspace"
96:         cmd="cd $nodeDataDir/data && find . -type d -print0 | grep -z -iE '/$keyspace/[^/]+/snapshots/$snapshotTag' | tar -cvzf $targetFolder/$keyspace/data.tar.gz --null -T -"
97:             echo "Executing: $cmd"
98:         if ! utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" "$cmd"; then
99:             echo "Failed to upload data for keyspace $keyspace"
100:             return 1
101:         fi
102:     done
103: }
104: 
105: dump_schema() {
106:     while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
107:         local keyspace="$1"
108:             shift
109:         cmd="docker exec $container cqlsh -e 'DESC KEYSPACE $keyspace' | grep -v '^$' | sed '/^Warning:/d' > $targetFolder/$keyspace/schema.cql"
110:         echo "Dump schema. Executing: $cmd"
111:         if ! utils_ssh -i "$sshKey" "$LOGNAME@$node" "$cmd"; then
112:             echo "Failed to dump schema for keyspace $keyspace"
113:             return 1
114:         fi
115:     done
116: }
117: 
118: backup() {
119:     signalFile create "$node"
120:     if container=$(getContainer "$containerName"); then
121:         echo "Container id for $containerName: $container"
122:     else
123:         echo "Failed to get Container id for $containerName"
124:     fi
125: 
126:     read -ra keyspaces <<< "$(descKeyspaces "$container")"
127: 
128:     echo "Init backup for node $node"
129:     for keyspace in "${keyspaces[@]}"; do
130:         echo "Keyspace: $keyspace"
131:     done
132: 
133:     snapshotTag=$(snapshotTag)
134:     if ! snapshotCtl snapshot; then
135:         echo "Failed to take snapshot"
136:         return 1
137:     fi
138: 
139:     upload "${keyspaces[@]}"
140:     dump_schema "${keyspaces[@]}"
141: }
142: 
143: function on_exit() {
144:     if [ -n "${snapshotTag:-}" ]; then
145:         snapshotCtl clearsnapshot
146:     fi
147:     signalFile remove "$node"
148: }
149: 
150: function on_error() {
151:     echo "Error occurred"
152:     on_exit
153: }
154: 
155: trap on_exit EXIT
156: trap on_error ERR
157: 
158: backup
159: 
160: exit 0

```go
func parseCronValue(s string, spec cronFieldSpec) (int, bool) {
	l := strings.ToLower(s)
	if v, ok := spec.names[l]; ok {
		return v, true
	}
	v, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
	return v, err == nil

func validCronItem(item string, spec cronFieldSpec) bool {
	if item == "*" {
		return true
	}

	step := 1
	// parse step "*/n" or "a-b/n"
	if idx := strings.Index(item, "/"); idx >= 0 {
		st, ok := parseCronValue(item[idx+1:], cronFieldSpec{1, 100, nil})  // hmm step can be any positive int
		if !ok || st <= 0 {
			return false
		}
		step = st
		item = item[:idx]
	}

	if item == "*" {
		return true
	}

	// range "a-b"
	if idx := strings.Index(item, "-"); idx >= 0 {
		from, ok1 := parseCronValue(item[:idx], spec)
		to, ok2 := parseCronValue(item[idx+1:], spec)
		if !ok1 || !ok2 {
			return false
		}
		return from <= to && from >= spec.min && to <= spec.max && step >= 1
	}

	// single value "a"
	v, ok := parseCronValue(item, spec)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	return v >= spec.min && v <= spec.max
}
```

```bash
# Copyright (c) 2023 Sigma-Soft, Ltd.
```

#
# Install the cron job that runs the database backup on the node where the script is executed.
# Usage: ./set-cron-backup.sh <cron expression>

# Operations:
#  - Remove the backup job from the crontab, if it already exists
#  - Add the new cron job that executes the backupnode.sh script

  echo "Usage: $0 <cron expression>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

backupScript="backupnode.sh"

(crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$backupScript" || true
echo "$cronExpr $backupCmd") | crontab -

echo "Cron job installed: '$cronExpr $backupCmd'"
